As of my last update in September 2021, Cao Yu is a prominent Chinese cinematographer known for his innovative techniques and significant contributions to contemporary Chinese cinema. Born on August 10, 1980, in Beijing, China, Cao Yu developed an interest in cinematography at a young age.

Cao Yu studied at the Beijing Film Academy, one of the largest film schools in Asia, where he honed his skills and developed a deep understanding of the craft of cinematography. Over the years, he has become known for his ability to capture intricate visual narratives, often using lighting and color to enhance the emotional and thematic depths of a film.

He gained international acclaim for his work on several notable films. One of his most prominent roles was as the cinematographer for the critically acclaimed film "City of Life and Death" (2009), directed by Lu Chuan. The film, which portrays the harrowing events of the Nanjing Massacre, was praised for its stark black and white cinematography, which Cao Yu masterfully used to portray the brutal reality of the historical events.

Cao Yu's collaboration with director Jia Zhangke has also been notably significant in his career. He worked as the cinematographer for Jia's "Mountains May Depart" (2015), a drama that explores China's past, present, and future through the lives of its characters. The film received positive reviews for its storytelling and visual style, showcasing Cao Yu's ability to adapt his cinematographic techniques to different narrative forms and settings.

In addition to feature films, Cao Yu has also worked in other formats, including short films and commercials, expanding his repertoire and adapting his cinematographic style to various forms of visual media. His work continues to influence and inspire new generations of filmmakers and cinematographers in China and around the world.

Cao Yu's cinematography is characterized by a meticulous attention to detail, a sensitive approach to lighting and color, and an ability to create compelling visual stories that complement and enhance the narrative and emotional impact of a film. His contributions have made him one of the leading cinematographers in Chinese cinema.
